turns.text: In your aiseasonlead-mid-task repository, specifically in app.py, you implemented a Flask server that runs an agent in a background thread and streams logs via Server-Sent Events. Could you explain your approach to managing thread safety and handling memory or job state cleanup via the _prune_jobs function in a production environment?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I used a lock to make sure only one thread updates the jobs dictionary at a time. _prune_jobs cleans up old entries so memory doesn't keep growing. In production I'd probably want something more robust than an in-memory dict, like a database.
